title: Milton Berle and his mouthpiece Johnny Bigle
summary: Berle came daily to hear Alan Drew, and Whaley says Berle's jokes came through Johnny Bigle, Clarence Robinson's partner and Berle's driver.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, tell me about some of those other guys. Let's see, Alan Drew and we talked about --

Milton Berle used to come to the theater, as I say, every day to listen to Alan Drew. And instead of Alan Drew cleaning up his stuff, like Milton did, becoming the greatest -- Johnny Bigle was Milton Berle's mouthpiece.
Did you know of Johnny Bigle?
Black boy. He used to drive Milton.

Yeah, he was a chauffeur, but he used to drive for Milton after he got out of show business, see. And he used to tell how Milton was so great. Oh, that's Johnny Bigle. Johnny Bigle used to tell them all that stuff. Drive him around nights and tell them all about how he and Clarence Robinson used to do things.
And perhaps he would tell them all of the stories.

Yeah, all the stuff. And when Johnny Bigle died, Milton Berle lost his mouthpiece. He tried to get a girl to do that, she couldn't do what Johnny Bigle -- and he lost a lot of precedence. But as long as Johnny Bigle was
living Show Milton Berle was the greatest.
